summary: Frontend-only verification of the React 'insertBefore / NotFoundError' crash fix in VideoPlayer.jsx, using the REAL YouTube IFrame API (no window.YT stub, per request). Logged in as tony@tonyyoga.com and exercised both reported lessons (/library/bcde4f96-... and /library/efa56e07-...). Confirmed the real YT API loaded and REPLACED the React-managed mount node (exactly 1 <iframe> inside [data-testid='video-youtube'], wrapper still has 4 stable children: mount-wrapper, ClipChip, play button, BottomBar). Then forced heavy overlay re-renders after the node replacement: custom play/pause x3, mute toggle x4, 3 clip-progress seeks, fullscreen enter/exit, resume-continue, SPA navigation A->B->A, and unmount-while-playing. RESULT: PASS on every criterion — 0 pageerror events, 0 console errors, no 'insertBefore'/'NotFoundError' anywhere, no CRA/react-error-overlay iframe, no 'Uncaught runtime errors' text, no white screen, and all custom controls (video-youtube, yt-toggle-play, clip-progress-track, player-mute, player-fullscreen, resume-banner, clip-duration-chip) present and interactive. The 'Video unavailable' YouTube frame in the sandbox is expected and does not affect the verdict.

Optional: handle the YT player 'onError' event so a genuinely unavailable/blocked video shows an app-level message instead of only YouTube's internal frame.

critical_code_review_comments: The fix is structurally correct: the YT mount div is the SOLE child of a stable absolutely-positioned wrapper, so React never has to reorder siblings across the node YouTube replaces. Keep it that way — adding any sibling inside that inner wrapper would reintroduce the crash.
loadYT() overwrites window.onYouTubeIframeAPIReady but chains the previous handler, and ytApiPromise is module-scoped — safe for repeat mounts (verified across A->B->A navigation).
The build effect guards with `cancelled` and `ytHostRef.current` before new YT.Player, and cleanup destroys the player + clears the poll interval; navigating away mid-play produced no errors.
VideoPlayer.jsx is ~470 lines with two near-duplicate control-overlay blocks (yt/native) — still worth extracting a shared <PlayOverlay/> (repeat of iterations 29/30 comment).

rca_of_the_issue: Original crash: the YouTube IFrame API physically replaces the React-managed mount <div> with its own <iframe>. That div was a direct sibling of the overlay elements (ClipChip / play button / BottomBar), so any overlay re-render (setPlaying on play, the 400ms clipPct poll, setMuted in onReady) made React call insertBefore referencing the now-detached mount node -> NotFoundError and a fatal dev overlay. Fix verified: the mount div is now the lone child of a stable absolutely-positioned wrapper and all overlays are siblings of that wrapper, so React never reorders siblings around the replaced node. No reproduction after 20+ overlay re-renders across both reported URLs.
